The Isle is one of those games that can be incredibly immersive and frustrating at the same time. The atmosphere, sound design, dinosaur animations, and feeling of actually surviving in a dangerous ecosystem are some of the best parts of the game. When everything works, exploring the map, growing your dinosaur, hunting, hiding, and interacting with other players can create some unforgettable moments.

However, the game still has a lot of problems. Performance can be inconsistent, bugs can ruin long sessions, and losing hours of progress because of something outside your control can be extremely frustrating. The development also feels very slow at times, and some mechanics still need more balancing and polish.

Despite all of that, there really isn't another dinosaur survival game that gives me the same feeling as The Isle. It has a huge amount of potential, and I keep coming back because when the game is good, it's genuinely amazing.

I just hope the developers continue improving performance, fixing bugs, and adding meaningful content without making players wait forever.

Overall: a unique and immersive survival experience with a lot of potential, but also a game that requires patience.

Two carnivores, one herbivore so far — already hooked. Atmosphere is why. Not a documentary, but the closest “real dinosaur” game I’ve played: fog, night, sound, something always watching. Above-water graphics are beautiful. Dino variety is good. This is a main game now; I’ll play daily and update this.
Finished Rex Prime in about two days. People quote ~30 hours; mine felt under 24 real hours. I did the hard grow first. Most of the roster is closer to ~6 hours. Fine on 1–2 species.
Survival is the hook and the pain. Prime is actually hard. I’ve failed it — starve, dumb deaths. Fair when it’s me. Less fair when the map eats you.
Stuck. Slide an edge, wedge in terrain, a lot. Logout/in usually saves you. Shouldn’t have to leave the game to climb a hill. Dilo doesn’t need a goat jump — fine. It should still step a small lip. Bouncing off a curb is funny and not “realistic.”

Rex on a busy server. Early life is everyone trying to eat you. 2–3 t is a bit better, still soft. Safer around 6 t / ~50%. Grindy. I don’t mind that once or twice.
Thin servers (5–20 online). High kg + contested pocket = they ate the AI, you gamble a new area blind. Survival veteran (18 years) — a +5–10% AI spawn would help without making it easy.
Deino / underwater. I want the croc to be good. You spend most of the life under the surface, and that world is empty. Murky void, little flora, little layout. Up top: fog, forests, night, landmarks. Down there: brown water and hope. Not asking for Subnautica. Even a ~30% pass — plants, logs, clearer shallows vs deep, places to hide — would make the biome match the rest of the game.
Baby hunt is worse. Small fish are almost uncatchable; they just leave. New Deino doesn’t get a readable loop: where to sit, how to line a bite, what is safe vs a big croc. You miss food, panic, swim into adults, quit. First hours should teach “creek, bank, sip, snap,” not “guess in the dark.” Kit can stay a croc. Underwater space and early fishing need work. Deino players: thumb this if you agree.
Servers. This is the other big limiter. What I can actually join is EU / US. From Asia the ping is rough — rubber-band bites, late Q reads, “I was already off that ledge,” fights that the other guy won on his screen. In a game this slow and this lethal, latency isn’t flavor. It decides grows.
Unofficial Asia boxes exist sometimes; they aren’t the same as official. Population splits, rules differ, you don’t know if the wipe or the admin lasts. A lot of us just eat 200 ms on official EU/US because that’s where people are.
Please add 1–2 dedicated official Asian servers. Even one full official and one overflow would change who can play this daily. Same rules, same patch, ping that matches the atmosphere you’re selling. Support the region the same way you support EU/US.
Polish: stuck spots, lips, food, zones, ping, official Asia, underwater art + baby Deino fishing. Bones are good. Don’t let a rock, an empty river, or 200 ms end the grow instead of a Rex.

AMAZING GAME. On paper. Very poor game in reality.

The game has an amazing concept and a lot of potential, but in its current state, the actual experience is extremely frustrating. It is riddled with bugs that can make the game borderline unplayable.

Some of the issues I've personally encountered include graphics becoming severely blurred and looking like Play-Doh, gore becoming unusable because organs won't detach or cannot be interacted with, organs becoming stuck in your mouth and preventing you from biting, eating, or drinking, and invisible AI that you can hear but cannot see. The invisible AI issue is a verified bug and one of the few issues the developers have acknowledged.

What makes these bugs worse is that there often isn't a simple in-game solution. Fixing them can require restarting the game, restarting the PC, or going into the local app data and deleting the game's config folder. Doing this also resets settings you may have customized. Having to resort to this repeatedly just to get basic gameplay mechanics working makes it very difficult to actually enjoy the game.

Unfortunately, my experience with the community has been almost as frustrating as the game itself. Criticism of the game, even legitimate criticism of documented bugs, can be met with extreme fanboyism and toxic positivity. Some members seem to treat criticism of the game or its developers as a personal attack, and discussions can quickly turn hostile.

What concerns me most is the moderation response to this behavior. From my experience, people who speak out about legitimate problems can end up being attacked by other members and, in some cases, removed from the Discord after responding to that hostility, with little or no avenue for appeal.

The PvP in the game can be toxic by nature. That's part of the territory. But that toxicity should stay in the PvP environment, not spill over into the game's community and discussions.

There is an amazing game buried underneath all of these problems. The concept, mechanics, and potential are genuinely impressive. But potential isn't the same thing as a good player experience. Until the game's major bugs are addressed and legitimate criticism can be discussed without the community turning on the person making it, I can't recommend the game in its current state.

The Good:

The Isle is a survival dino game that promises to take you from an egg to a apex adult. You'll eat, drink, fight, raise children, and die. Gameplay loop is short and satisfying. Most sessions can be completed in 30-45 mins or whenever you wish by putting your dino to sleep and picking it back up tomorrow.  This game has potential for novel experiences with others online and can really be fun for imaginative play. 

The Bad:
This game has been in EA for a long time. It suffers from most problems that plague similar projects. The premise is interesting but the scope of the game is limited to the gameplay patterns of internet players. So expect griefing, immersion breaking bugs, and hope for how things could go but realizing how they will go. 

The Ugly:
By far the worst issue facing The Isle is the direction toward version 1. For all intent and purpose that direction and development is currently going nowhere. Don't fool yourself into thinking this game will "get better" once "it's finished". It probably will never feel "finished" because the problem with creating a game with survival is deciding where to stop reality and where to start the gameplay. I don't play roblox but my kids do. This game feels like a Roblox game made in unreal 5. But for many that is completely fine. 

Discussion:
Most games that are in development are canceled. Some games are stuck in development hell. Many are pruned and shipped too quickly or approved by a board of executives that grind down all the edges and ship a smooth game. Few games are gems to be cherished. The individual decides which games they find the most appealing. This is another problem with the Isle. 

The game has been out and in early access for years. There will be many versions of the game or directions of the game that never materialized passed the planning stages. The player base will likely splinter into these game versions. Do you like the Isle? This game has the "yes but.." problem that many EA games have. "I like the game but... what if the dino's had mutations!!" some people love the "but" of developers or random community feedback but other people hate that and what something else entirely. 

In conclusion: Get this game if you want a sandbox dino game with survival elements. Expect to play a dino game hunting for food, drinking water, and dying to other players(or killing others if that is your thing). 

Compare the dev cycle of 7 days to die to the Isle and don't expect a polished experience. For some gamers this is exactly the type of game they want. And hell I had fun with my time with the game.  I'd say most people wont like this game tho and because of that i don't really recommend it.

I’ve been watching The Isle for quite a while but never actually pulled the trigger on buying it until recently. I really wish I had picked it up sooner.

For a dinosaur survival game, this is way more in-depth than I expected. It’s not just running around as a dinosaur and attacking everything you see. You have to worry about food, water, growth, injuries, bleeding, diets, migration, where you’re going, what’s around you, and whether the dinosaur you just spotted is going to leave you alone or ruin the last hour of progress.

I really like that every dinosaur feels like it has its own playstyle instead of just being a different skin with different stats. There’s actually a learning curve, and figuring out your abilities, attacks, diet, and how to survive as each species is a big part of the game.

The atmosphere is also really good. Walking through the forest and hearing something nearby that you can’t see yet genuinely makes you nervous. Playing with friends makes it even better, especially when you’re trying to keep the group together, find food, and survive whatever comes across you.

The game definitely isn’t perfect and there are still things that can be frustrating, but overall I’ve been extremely impressed with how much depth there is here.

If you like dinosaurs, survival games, and games that actually make you learn how to survive instead of holding your hand, I definitely recommend The Isle.

**Title:** A High-Potential Game Broken by Server Instability and Cheaters

**Rating:** 2/5 Stars

I put 142 hours into *The Isle*, and at its core, it is a genuinely fun and unique game. I particularly enjoyed playing as the Deinosuchus. However, as someone with a job and kids, my gaming time is extremely limited, and right now, the game feels like a complete waste of time.

**Major Technical Issues:**

* **Performance:** Severe FPS drops, latency spikes, and frequent ping issues ruin the gameplay.
* **Server Instability:** Constant crashes lead to losing hours of hard-earned progress. At one point, progress was practically wiped on a daily basis.
* **Broken AI:** Animal and fish AI rarely spawn properly, leaving you to starve before you even have a chance to survive.

**The Dealbreaker:**
Growing an apex predator like the Deinosuchus takes massive time and patience. Spending hours raising an avatar, only to be killed by fresh-spawn cheaters, completely destroys the experience.

As content creators and the community have pointed out, the cheating epidemic on official servers has only worsened recently due to poor moderation and weak anti-cheat. I haven't logged back on since my last encounter with a hacker, and I can't recommend *The Isle* to anyone who values their time.

I've only been playing for a few days now, but I have really been enjoying things so far. Just know a few things going in:
-No Hand Holding. YouTube is your friend, learn from there and if you are lucky, players will help you... instead of, or before they eat you. Seriously tho, Very little in-game help, so look elsewhere.
- Verify you change the default version in steam to the new version once you have downloaded the game.
- Research your servers. Skip the official servers in my opinion, the unofficial (selectable from a drop down in the server menu) are much better, and seem better moderated. But, I suggest looking for the server you are thinking about, check out their discord channel/website look at their rules, see if it is what you are comfortable with.
- You Will Die. There is no getting around it. This is a survival game with a core PVP element. You will die. It might be right after you spawn and make your way to the first watering hole you see, or it might be right before your dino is about to die from old age (happened to me yesterday). Make peace with that fact. What I can say from my own personal experience, PVP and getting killed in this game is not like other MMORPG's I've been in where once someone has killer gear, they are near unstoppable and other players just enjoy griefing folks. That's not really the experience I've had in this game. You live and die based very much on species interaction, growth and mutation status, and a lot of luck (right/wrong place, right/wrong time). The point is, anyone can be taken down. And should you achieve that status of Prime (look it up, they are cool) you can enjoy it, but know, even if you don't lose a fight, your dino will die of old age. So, there is no peak that people stay at and dominate younger dinos from.  So, that, to my mind, is why the PVP is not a bad thing in this game.
-Last thing, have fun with it. This is still a game, and honestly what made me want to play was watching the folks who stream their games and seeing the fun they were having, and not just them, but all the people they meet and interact with. It's a Dinosaur game folks, revel in that!

So, yea, do your research, watch your videos, and take the plunge. I can honestly say, that even with only a few days under my belt, I feel like it was $20 well spend. Hope you enjoy it!
